Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
revision_notes: Confirmed via Data Protection Africa (2022) and RTP Africa news (Feb 2025) that Guinea-Bissau still has no comprehensive data protection law; the government has expressed intent to draft such legislation but no bill has been enacted or formally tabled. Lower-quality secondary sources (Generis Online, LawGratis) reference a "draft" law in development but contain internal inconsistencies (e.g. claiming an active National Data Protection Authority despite stating no law exists) and are not treated as authoritative. Score of 1 = No legislation confirmed; original source and score stand.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau has not enacted comprehensive data protection or privacy legislation. The Data Protection Africa factsheet records no data protection law and no appointed data protection authority, and reporting from February 2025 confirms the government is still seeking to develop such legislation rather than having adopted it. The Information Society Law (Law No. 5/2010) addresses telecommunications and internet governance but does not constitute a data protection framework.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
Comments: <10%; 1.89M kWh renewables out of low total production. Now hydro import but low share. [[IEA via Global Economy](https://www.theglobaleconomy.com/Guinea-Bissau/Electricity_from_renewable_sources_kWh/)]
revision_notes: Confirmed. Countryeconomy.com generation statistics show renewable electricity generation at 3.97% of total generation in 2024, up only marginally from around 3.5% in 2021-2023, consistent with the original <10% band. IRENA's 2025 renewable energy statistics likewise show negligible absolute renewable capacity/generation for Guinea-Bissau. Score of 1 = <10% confirmed with fresher data; original source (TheGlobalEconomy/IEA, 2021) was consistent but dated.
revised_comments: Renewable sources contribute a very small share of Guinea-Bissau's electricity generation, estimated at under 4% of total generation in 2024. Generation capacity remains dominated by imported and thermal power, with only a small hydro and solar contribution, placing the country well below 10% renewable share of generation.

Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
Comments: None listed in AfriLabs/Briter Bridges (0 hubs). [[AfriLabs Report](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/574977573)]
revision_notes: The original score (1 = none identified, based on a 2019 AfriLabs report showing zero hubs) is out of date. Two active, identifiable technology/innovation hubs now operate in Guinea-Bissau: InnovaLab (established 2015; 10+ years running incubation, accelerator and think-tank programmes; 300+ events and workshops; 10,000+ people trained) and Impact Hub Bissau / Kau Criar (active for 4+ years; mentoring, events and financing support; an active community of around 50 members and ongoing training programmes). This matches the "1-2 hubs with limited activity" band (score 2) rather than "none identified" (score 1). Not a top-of-scale change, so no escalation required.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau has a small but active innovation hub scene, anchored by two identifiable organisations. InnovaLab is a Bissau-based innovation and entrepreneurship think tank and accelerator running since 2015, with a track record of hundreds of events and thousands of people trained. Impact Hub Bissau manages the Kau Criar innovation and entrepreneurship centre, offering mentoring, events and financing support to a community of local start-ups. Activity remains limited in scale relative to larger regional ecosystems.
